tools.name: whoami
tools.description:
Show the currently authenticated user and server URL.

Validates the stored session token by calling the Strada API. If the
session is expired or invalid, run `strada login` again.

tools.name: orgs_list
tools.description:
List all organizations you belong to.

Shows org name, role, and ID. A green dot marks the org configured for
the current folder. If no org is configured, run `strada setup`.

tools.name: setup
tools.description:
Save the default organization and project for the current folder.

Strada resolves config by walking up from the current directory and using
the closest matching scope. Use this once per app folder so commands like
`strada logs` and `strada issues list` do not need `-p`.

scope.description: Directory scope to configure (default: current directory)

project.description: Project slug or ID

tools.name: projects_list
tools.description:
List all projects in the current organization.

Shows project slugs and IDs. Use the slug with -p in other commands.
Slugs often include an environment suffix (e.g. 'my-app-prod').
This also refreshes the local project cache.

tools.name: projects_create
tools.description:
Create a new project and generate its first org-wide ingest token.

The generated project ID becomes the ingest hostname: `{projectId}-ingest.strada.sh`.
The token printed at creation is shown only once. Save it as `STRADA_TOKEN`
for server-side SDKs. Browser SDKs do not need a token.

logsDays.description: Log and custom-event retention in days

allDays.description: Set all four signals to the same number of days

tools.name: projects_delete
tools.description:
Delete a project by its ID.

This removes the project from D1. Data already ingested into
Tinybird/ClickHouse is not deleted. Get the project ID from
`strada projects list`.

tools.name: projects_retention
tools.description:
Show raw telemetry retention for a project.

Traces default to 14 days, logs to 30 days, errors and metrics to 90 days.
`--logs-days` also controls custom product events stored in `otel_logs`.
Aggregated browser analytics and health-check results stay at a fixed 90 days.
Issue state and identified users are kept.

Per-project custom values require a Tinybird backend. Self-hosted ClickHouse
uses the static defaults in `clickhouse.sql`.

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: issues_list
tools.description:
List error issue groups sorted by frequency.

Groups errors by FingerprintHash and shows the count, exception type,
message, status, and last seen time for each group. This is the starting
point for debugging production errors. Use --since to control the time
range and -s to filter by service.

After finding an issue, copy its fingerprint hash and run
`strada issues view <fingerprint>` to see the full stack trace and
recent events.

By default only 'open' issues are shown. Use `--status` to filter by
triage state: open, resolved, muted, ignored, or all.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

status.description: Filter by triage status: open, resolved, muted, ignored, all (default: open)

tools.name: issues_view
tools.description:
Show full details for a single issue by fingerprint hash.

Displays exception type, message, stack trace (structured frames when
available), triage status, mechanism (handled/unhandled), services,
releases, environments, and a table of recent error events with trace
correlation IDs.

Get the fingerprint hash from `strada issues list`. The `--events` flag
controls how many recent occurrences to show (default 5).

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

events.description: Number of recent error events to show (default: 5)

tools.name: issues_resolve
tools.description:
Mark an issue as resolved.

Sets the issue status to 'resolved' in otel_issue_state. Resolved issues
are hidden from the default `strada issues list` output. Use `--status all`
or `--status resolved` to see them. Reopen with `strada issues unresolve`.

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: issues_mute
tools.description:
Mark an issue as muted.

Muted issues still collect error events but are hidden from the default
`strada issues list` output. Use `--status muted` or `--status all` to see them.
Useful for known noise you want to triage separately.

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: issues_unresolve
tools.description:
Reopen a resolved or muted issue.

Sets the status back to 'open' so it appears in the default listing again.

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: issues_assign
tools.description:
Assign an issue to an org member or remove the current assignee.

Pass `--to <member-id>` to assign, or `--unassign` to clear the assignee.
Get member IDs from the Strada website team page.

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_pages
tools.description:
Top pages by pageviews from the otel_analytics_pages materialized view.

Shows pathname, pageview count, and unique visitor count. Uses
countMerge/uniqMerge for AggregatingMergeTree columns.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_browsers
tools.description: Top browsers by unique visitors

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_devices
tools.description: Top device types by unique visitors

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_countries
tools.description: Top countries by unique visitors

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_referrers
tools.description: Top traffic sources by unique visitors

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_languages
tools.description: Top browser languages by unique visitors

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_kpis
tools.description:
Summary KPIs: unique visitors, pageviews, sessions, bounce rate, and
average session duration.

Unique visitors come from `visitor.id` (cookie `strada_vid`, survives tabs and logout). Sessions
come from `session.id` (one tab). Query both MVs. Use this as a health
check of browser analytics. Same numbers as `strada analytics overview`.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_overview
tools.description:
One-screen browser analytics: unique visitors, pageviews, sessions,
bounce rate, top pages, and top referrers.

Same numbers as `strada analytics kpis` plus the first few rows of
`strada analytics pages` and `strada analytics referrers`. Use this
instead of writing SQL for a daily traffic check.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_timeseries
tools.description:
Daily unique visitors and pageviews.

Reads `otel_analytics_pages` grouped by Date. Use this for growth
charts without writing SQL. `--since 30d` is the usual window.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_visitors
tools.description:
Unique visitors, first visits, and returning visitors.

Unique visitors are `visitor.id` (cookie `strada_vid`). First visits are unique
visitors whose first pageview is in the same date window, from the pages MV
`FirstVisits` column. Returning = unique minus first. Older data without
`visitor.id` still counts via `session.id` fallback.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_events
tools.description: Top custom events by occurrence count

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: analytics_realtime
tools.description:
Count active visitors in the last 5 minutes.

Queries raw otel_traces for pageview spans with distinct session.id
values. This is a real-time metric, not from the materialized views.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: query
tools.description:
Run a ClickHouse SQL query against a project's database.

Without a FORMAT clause, renders an auto-sized terminal table. Add `--json`
to get the raw JSON envelope `{ data, meta, rows, statistics }` instead.

Append a ClickHouse FORMAT clause to the SQL for raw output: JSON,
JSONEachRow, CSV, CSVWithNames, TSV, TSVWithNames, PrettyCompact,
Parquet, Prometheus. The response body is written directly to stdout
so you can pipe it.

ProjectId filtering is automatic via JWT. Never add `WHERE ProjectId` in SQL.

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

json.description: Print the raw JSON envelope { data, meta, rows, statistics } instead of a table (only applies when no FORMAT clause is in the SQL)

tools.name: alerts_create
tools.description:
Create an error alert rule.

Alert when errors of the same fingerprint exceed a threshold within
a time window. Multiple rules per org are supported. Project-scoped
rules override org-wide rules for the same project.

Optionally pass --channel and --to to create a destination inline.
All existing org destinations are auto-linked to the new rule.

project.description: Scope to a project (omit for all projects)

tools.name: alerts_list
tools.description:
Show all alert rules and destinations for the current org.

Lists both error_threshold and health_check rules with their
destinations. Use `strada checks list` to see health check details.

tools.name: alerts_update
tools.description:
Update an error alert rule's settings.

Change the threshold, window, cooldown, or name of an existing
error_threshold rule. Get the rule ID from `strada alerts list`.

tools.name: alerts_delete
tools.description:
Delete an error alert rule.

Destinations are not deleted; they remain for other rules.
Get the rule ID from `strada alerts list`.

tools.name: alerts_test
tools.description:
Send a test alert to all destinations in the org.

Verifies that each destination (email, webhook) is reachable.

tools.name: checks_create
tools.description:
Create a URL health check that runs on a schedule.

The check fetches the URL with the specified method and expects a status
code in the configured range (default 200-299). After N consecutive
failures (default 2), alerts fire to all configured destinations.

Checks auto-disable after continuous failure for `--auto-disable-hours`
(default 24) to avoid filling the database with identical failure rows.
Re-enable with `strada checks enable <id>`.

Alerts go to the same destinations as error alerts. If no destinations
are configured, add one first with `strada alerts create`.

autoDisableHours.description: Auto-disable after N hours of failure, 0 to disable (default: 24)

project.description: Project slug to scope the check to

tools.name: checks_list
tools.description:
List all health checks for the current org.

Shows check name, URL, schedule, status, and whether it's enabled.
Use `strada checks delete <id>` to remove a check.

tools.name: checks_delete
tools.description:
Delete a health check by ID.

Removes the check rule from D1. Historical check results remain in
ClickHouse and are queryable via `strada query`.

tools.name: checks_enable
tools.description:
Re-enable a health check that was disabled (manually or auto-disabled).

Auto-disabled checks stop running after continuous failure for too long.
Re-enable them so they start checking again.

tools.name: checks_disable
tools.description:
Manually disable a health check.

The check stops running but the rule is preserved. Re-enable with
`strada checks enable <id>`.

tools.name: destinations_list
tools.description:
List all notification destinations for the current org.

Destinations receive both error alerts and health check alerts.
They are auto-linked to all alert rules in the org.

tools.name: destinations_remove
tools.description:
Remove a notification destination.

Unlinks the destination from all alert rules and deletes it.
Get the destination ID from `strada destinations list` or `strada alerts list`.

tools.name: logs
tools.description:
Browse and search OTel log records from otel_logs.

Renders one log per line with timestamp, severity, service, body, and
attributes. Supports subcommands: `list` (default) and `stats`.

Use `-w` for raw SQL WHERE filters on attribute maps.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

since.description: Start time: duration (1h, 7d) or ISO date (default: 1h)

until.description: End time: duration (1h) or ISO date

minLevel.description: Minimum severity: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal

traceId.description: Show logs for a specific trace

tools.name: services_list
tools.description:
Find service names that are actively generating logs or traces.

Use this before filtering logs, issues, or SQL queries by ServiceName.
It helps discover the real service.name values present in a project and
shows which services are currently producing telemetry in the selected
time range.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

since.description: Start time: duration (1h, 7d) or ISO date (default: 24h)

until.description: End time: duration (1h) or ISO date

tools.name: traces_list
tools.description:
List distributed traces in a project, grouped by TraceId.

Use this to find trace IDs before running `strada traces view`.
Scans otel_traces in the selected time range, summarizes span counts,
services, error spans, duration, and the first root span when one exists.
Project isolation is enforced by the project-scoped query API.

project.description: Project slug override (repeatable, defaults to folder setup)

since.description: Start time: duration (1h, 7d) or ISO date (default: 1h)

until.description: End time: duration (1h) or ISO date

errors.description: Only show traces with error spans

tools.name: traces_span
tools.description:
Show the full details for one span inside a trace.

Use the short span id printed by `strada traces view`, or paste a full
SpanId. The command prints all span attributes, resource attributes,
scope attributes, exception events, and links without truncation. Use this
after the compact tree has identified the span that needs inspection.

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

tools.name: traces_view
tools.description:
Render one distributed trace as a parent-child span tree.

Use a TraceId from `strada traces list` or from logs/errors. The SQL
fetches all spans for that TraceId, then the CLI builds a SpanNode tree
from SpanId and ParentSpanId. Use `--json` to print a shape designed to
match the @strada.sh/ui trace timeline, making future code sharing simple.

project.description: Project slug override (defaults to folder setup)

attrs.description: Number of compact span attributes to show

expandSpan.description: SpanId or unique SpanId prefix to expand (repeatable)

tools.name: tokens_create
tools.description:
Create an org-wide token with an explicit scope.

Tokens with the ingest scope authenticate writes to the OTLP collector only. They do
not grant query access, project management access, or access to the
Strada website API. Use them in Node.js, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, and
other trusted server runtimes.

The only supported scope today is `ingest`. The scope is still required
as `--scope` so command usage will stay stable when more token scopes are
added later.

Browser SDKs should not use tokens. Browser ingest stays
anonymous and is protected by the collector's anonymous rate limit.

scope.description: Token scope. Currently only ingest is supported

tools.name: tokens_list
tools.description:
List org-wide tokens.

This shows token metadata and prefixes only. Full token values are never
stored by Strada and cannot be recovered after creation. Create a new
token and delete the old one when rotating credentials.

tools.name: tokens_delete
tools.description:
Delete an org-wide token.

Use this to rotate leaked or obsolete server-side ingestion credentials.
Deleting a token immediately stops future collector requests that use it.
